edits.find: A 5-pound bag of shredded cheese might cost $18, or $3.60 a pound. Your grocery store puts 2-pound bags on sale for $6, or $3.00 a pound. The smaller sale bag wins.
edits.replace: A 5-pound bag of shredded cheese can cost more per pound than the 2-pound bags your grocery store puts on sale. When it does, the smaller sale bag wins.
edits.why: a hypothetical two-package comparison; one live cell cannot show two package sizes, so the lesson stays in words

edits.find: Run the numbers on that 5-pound bag of spring mix that cost $9. If half of it turns to slime in the crisper drawer before you eat it, you did not pay $9 for greens. You paid $9 for the greens you actually ate, which means your real cost doubled to the equivalent of $18 for the usable half.
edits.replace: Run the numbers on a 5-pound bag of spring mix. If half of it turns to slime in the crisper drawer before you eat it, you did not pay that price for five pounds of greens. You paid it for the greens you actually ate, which means your real cost per pound doubled for the usable half.
edits.why: a hypothetical 5-pound bulk bag; the spring-mix cell prices small clamshells, not that bag, so the waste arithmetic stays in words
